key_insight: The paper proposes training LLM agents to proactively reorganize raw documents into reusable workspaces that anticipate future questions, rather than relying only on reactive retrieval at inference time.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a new systems pattern for long-context AI: spend compute upfront to build structured, query-ready file hierarchies that reduce latency and improve multi-document reasoning later.
method: Builder agent turns unstructured corpora into a hierarchical filesystem of synthetic files and reference links.
Workspace construction is framed as a Markov decision process.
The builder is trained with reinforcement learning to maximize downstream answering accuracy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 33-point gain on BrowseComp-Plus and a 31-point average accuracy improvement on BRIGHT, indicating strong gains from the learned workspace construction approach.
watch_item: The approach adds upfront construction overhead and may depend on reliable filesystem-like tooling and careful reward design to avoid brittle or overfitted workspace structures.
paper_title: Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries
